subject: Finishes that connect living spaces
hook: The edge is where cheap furniture gives itself away.
ig:
The edge is where cheap furniture gives itself away.

Look along the side of a shelf or door. If you see a pale line, a slightly different shade, or edging lifting at a corner, the finish stops there and so does the illusion.

On our furniture, panels are edged in our own workshop with ABS edging chosen to match the board. That gives you:

- The same colour and grain look on face and edge, so an oak-effect sideboard reads as oak-effect from every angle
- Edging that suits where the panel sits: thinner on hidden edges, thicker on fronts that take knocks
- Clean, trimmed corners rather than overhangs that catch on clothes

It matters even more in open-plan rooms, where you see furniture from the side as you walk past.

Which edge in your house takes the most punishment? Tell us in the comments.
fb:
Next time you walk past a sideboard or bookcase, look at the edge rather than the front. That's where you can tell how carefully it's been made.

We edge every panel in our Hanley workshop with ABS edging matched to the board, thicker on the edges that get knocked and neatly trimmed at the corners, so the finish carries all the way round. In an open-plan room you see furniture side-on all the time, so it's worth getting right.

Have a look at our sideboards and drop us a message if you've got a space in mind.
